properties.title: Liberica Coffee Seedling and Nursery Training – Pedekik Village
properties.description:
Pelatihan Penyemaian dan Pembibitan Kopi Liberika dilaksanakan pada 17 Juni 2026 di Kantor Desa Pedekik, Kecamatan Bengkalis, Kabupaten Bengkalis. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan kapasitas masyarakat dalam pengembangan Kopi Liberika sebagai komoditas ramah gambut sekaligus mendukung restorasi ekosistem gambut dan pengurangan risiko kebakaran lahan.

Pelatihan diikuti oleh 36 peserta, terdiri dari 26 laki-laki dan 10 perempuan, yang berasal dari Kelompok Pedekik Lestari, Pemerintah Desa Pedekik, Kecamatan Bengkalis, Mapala Laksamana, dan masyarakat Desa Pedekik. Materi pelatihan mencakup konservasi gambut, penerapan Zero Burning, pengelolaan Tinggi Muka Air Tanah (TMAT), teknik penyemaian dan pembibitan Kopi Liberika, sistem agroforestri, serta penguatan ekonomi masyarakat berbasis komoditas ramah gambut.

Sambutan disampaikan oleh Pj. Kepala Desa Pedekik, Syaiful Anwar, dan Camat Bengkalis, Rafli Kurniawan, yang menekankan pentingnya pengembangan Kopi Liberika sebagai komoditas unggulan lahan gambut melalui kolaborasi antara pemerintah, masyarakat, dan lembaga mitra. Materi teknis disampaikan oleh Raja Alpian (Yayasan Gambut) mengenai pengelolaan gambut berkelanjutan, restorasi hidrologi, pembukaan lahan tanpa bakar, dan penerapan agroforestri, serta Tuti Kelana dari Kelompok Wanita Tani Makmur Jaya yang berbagi pengalaman praktik pembibitan dan pemberdayaan masyarakat.

Pelatihan diharapkan menjadi langkah awal pengembangan pusat pembibitan Kopi Liberika di Desa Pedekik sebagai bagian dari upaya restorasi gambut berbasis masyarakat dan peningkatan mata pencaharian yang berkelanjutan.

properties.title: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme – Kelapa Pati
properties.description: Community-based mangrove planting and environmental education activity implemented by Yayasan Gambut and Global Environment Centre (GEC) with support from Aramco Asia Singapore in Kelapa Pati Village, Bengkalis Regency. The event involved 67 participants, including local government representatives, community groups, university students, school students, and partner organizations. During the activity, 200 mangrove trees (Rhizophora apiculata and Rhizophora stylosa) were planted, increasing the cumulative total to 6,200 trees across approximately 3 hectares of restored mangrove area. The programme also promoted community-based livelihood development through mangrove products, environmental education, and ecotourism initiatives, strengthening long-term community stewardship for coastal ecosystem restoration.

properties.title: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme
properties.description:
The third day of the programme continued with a mangrove tree planting event at SDN 17 Bukit Batu in Buruk Bakul, Riau Province, a site established under Phase 1 (2024/2025) and further expanded through Phase 2 (2025/2026). The event was officiated by Pak Acil Esyno, Head of Bukit Batu Subdistrict, bringing together local government, community groups, schools, and partner organisations. Pak Mul (YG) and Mr. Nagarajan Rengasamy, Manager of the Forest and Coastal Programme at GEC, presented programme progress, highlighting restoration achievements, community participation, and the programme's environmental and socio-economic impacts. Pak Acil Esyno commended the Sekat Bakau community for its innovative efforts in mangrove restoration and its growing contribution to sustainable coastal rehabilitation.

Prior to the event, 22,000 mangrove trees had been planted at the site: 8,000 under Phase 1, 10,000 under Phase 2, and 4,000 under Phase 3. Today's activity targeted the planting of 200 trees, comprising Teruntum Putih (Lumnitzera racemosa) and Tumu Merah (Bruguiera gymnorhiza). Of these, 100 trees were planted within the school compound today, with the remaining 100 to be planted at the restoration site tomorrow. Planting was conducted within the school grounds to ensure participant safety while creating a greener learning environment and strengthening students' appreciation of mangrove ecosystems. Upon completion of the two-day activity, the cumulative total at Buruk Bakul will reach 4,200 trees under Phase 3, bringing the overall total across Phases 1–3 to 22,200 mangrove trees.

The Sekat Bakau Community Group also showcased and sold products developed through knowledge and skills gained from a peer learning visit to Malaysia and capacity-building activities under Phase 2, enabling members to diversify their livelihoods and generate additional income. Building on these achievements, the site is progressing toward community-based mangrove ecotourism and serving as a living outdoor classroom for mangrove environmental education. Through continued environmental awareness, innovation, and strong community participation, the Buruk Bakul model stands as a practical reference that could inspire and inform similar community-led mangrove conservation and livelihood initiatives across other coastal areas in Bengkalis.

properties.title: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme
properties.description:
The fourth day of the programme continued with a mangrove tree planting event at Desa Sepahat, Riau Province, a new restoration site established under Phase 3 (2025/2026). The site has experienced significant coastal erosion in recent years, resulting in shoreline retreat and loss of coastal habitat, underscoring the urgent need for continued mangrove rehabilitation to stabilise the coastline and protect surrounding communities. Facing directly onto the Malacca Strait, the site required a different planting method, which has proven effective through sustained engagement with the Sepahat Hijau Community Group.

The event was officiated by Pak Risky Afriandy, Head of Bandar Laksamana Subdistrict, bringing together local government agencies, community groups, schools, and partner organisations. Pak Mul, Director of YG, and Mr. Nagarajan Rengasamy, Manager of the Forest and Coastal Programme at GEC, presented programme progress, highlighting restoration achievements, community participation, and the environmental and socio-economic benefits generated through the initiative. Pak Risky Afriandy commended the Sepahat Hijau Community Group for its innovative approach to mangrove restoration and its growing contribution to sustainable coastal rehabilitation.

Prior to the event, 4,000 mangrove trees had been planted under Phase 3. Latest monitoring shows more than 3,000 trees have survived, demonstrating encouraging establishment despite challenging coastal conditions; GEC has also provided further guidance to improve survival rates in this area. To strengthen restoration efforts, participants planted an additional 200 mangrove trees as replacement planting, comprising Perepat ( Sonneratia alba ) and Api-api Putih ( Avicennia alba ).

The Sepahat Hijau Community Group showcased and marketed its wild honey with improved packaging and branding, developed through a peer learning visit to Malaysia and capacity-building activities under Phase 2. The enhanced product has increased marketability, creating additional income opportunities for community members. Alongside these livelihood initiatives, the community actively addresses severe coastal erosion through mangrove restoration and coastal rehabilitation. The Sepahat model demonstrates how conservation, sustainable livelihoods, and strong community participation can strengthen coastal resilience and could inspire similar initiatives across Bengkalis Regency.

properties.title: Pelatihan Pembibitan Kopi Liberika di Desa Dayun
properties.description: Kegiatan Pelatihan Pembibitan Kopi Liberika Di Desa Dayun dilaksanakan pada tanggal 25 Juli 2026 di Balai Pertemuan Desa Dayun, Kabupaten Siak. Sebanyak 43 orang peserta yang meliputi kelompok tani, kelompok perhutanan sosial, dan masyarakat setempat. Pelatihan ini diadakan untuk merespons keterbatasan pengetahuan masyarakat mengenai teknik budidaya kopi Liberika yang adaptif di lahan gambut, dengan tujuan meningkatkan kapasitas mereka dalam menerapkan sistem pertanian berkelanjutan yang mampu mendiversifikasi pendapatan ekonomi dan mendukung mitigasi deforestasi tanpa harus membuka kawasan hutan baru. Untuk mencapai tujuan tersebut, kegiatan ini dilaksanakan selama satu hari penuh melalui metode ceramah interaktif, diskusi kelompok, tanya jawab, dan sharing pengalaman bersama narasumber ahli, di mana peserta akan dibekali materi komprehensif mulai dari teknis pembibitan dan perawatan kopi hingga implementasi konsep agroforestri di lahan gambut.

properties.title: Rapid Monitoring Pasca Penanaman Mangrove Fase 3 – Desa Buruk Bakul
properties.description: Monitoring pasca penanaman Mangrove Fase 3 di Desa Buruk Bakul untuk mengevaluasi tingkat keberhasilan penanaman, pertumbuhan bibit, serta kondisi areal restorasi. Monitoring dilakukan melalui pengukuran tinggi tanaman, diameter batang, jumlah daun, dan persentase hidup tanaman.
properties.Ancaman: Belum ditemukan ancaman yang signifikan. Tidak terdapat abrasi, gelombang ekstrem maupun sampah kiriman yang mempengaruhi pertumbuhan bibit.
properties.Temuan: Monitoring terhadap areal penanaman Mangrove Fase 3 sebanyak 4.000 batang menunjukkan kondisi pertumbuhan yang sangat baik. Tingkat kelangsungan hidup mencapai 100% dengan tinggi bibit rata-rata 30–40 cm, diameter batang 1,0–1,4 cm, dan jumlah daun 6–8 helai. Bibit tumbuh sehat, seragam, serta tidak ditemukan kerusakan yang berarti. Kondisi tapak masih stabil dan mendukung pertumbuhan mangrove.

properties.title: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme – Kelapa Pati
properties.description: Community-based mangrove planting and environmental education activity implemented by Yayasan Gambut and Global Environment Centre (GEC) with support from Aramco Asia Singapore in Kelapa Pati Village, Bengkalis Regency. The event involved 67 participants, including local government representatives, community groups, university students, school students, and partner organizations. During the activity, 200 mangrove trees (Rhizophora apiculata and Rhizophora stylosa) were planted, increasing the cumulative total to 6,200 trees across approximately 3 hectares of restored mangrove area. The programme also promoted community-based livelihood development through mangrove products, environmental education, and ecotourism initiatives, strengthening long-term community stewardship for coastal ecosystem restoration.

properties.Nama_Objek: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme
properties.title: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme
properties.description:
The third day of the programme continued with a mangrove tree planting event at SDN 17 Bukit Batu in Buruk Bakul, Riau Province, a site established under Phase 1 (2024/2025) and further expanded through Phase 2 (2025/2026). The event was officiated by Pak Acil Esyno, Head of Bukit Batu Subdistrict, bringing together local government, community groups, schools, and partner organisations. Pak Mul (YG) and Mr. Nagarajan Rengasamy, Manager of the Forest and Coastal Programme at GEC, presented programme progress, highlighting restoration achievements, community participation, and the programme's environmental and socio-economic impacts. Pak Acil Esyno commended the Sekat Bakau community for its innovative efforts in mangrove restoration and its growing contribution to sustainable coastal rehabilitation.

Prior to the event, 22,000 mangrove trees had been planted at the site: 8,000 under Phase 1, 10,000 under Phase 2, and 4,000 under Phase 3. Today's activity targeted the planting of 200 trees, comprising Teruntum Putih (Lumnitzera racemosa) and Tumu Merah (Bruguiera gymnorhiza). Of these, 100 trees were planted within the school compound today, with the remaining 100 to be planted at the restoration site tomorrow. Planting was conducted within the school grounds to ensure participant safety while creating a greener learning environment and strengthening students' appreciation of mangrove ecosystems. Upon completion of the two-day activity, the cumulative total at Buruk Bakul will reach 4,200 trees under Phase 3, bringing the overall total across Phases 1–3 to 22,200 mangrove trees.

The Sekat Bakau Community Group also showcased and sold products developed through knowledge and skills gained from a peer learning visit to Malaysia and capacity-building activities under Phase 2, enabling members to diversify their livelihoods and generate additional income. Building on these achievements, the site is progressing toward community-based mangrove ecotourism and serving as a living outdoor classroom for mangrove environmental education. Through continued environmental awareness, innovation, and strong community participation, the Buruk Bakul model stands as a practical reference that could inspire and inform similar community-led mangrove conservation and livelihood initiatives across other coastal areas in Bengkalis.

properties.Nama_Objek: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme
properties.title: Mangrove Tree Planting and Community Engagement Programme
properties.description:
The fourth day of the programme continued with a mangrove tree planting event at Desa Sepahat, Riau Province, a new restoration site established under Phase 3 (2025/2026). The site has experienced significant coastal erosion in recent years, resulting in shoreline retreat and loss of coastal habitat, underscoring the urgent need for continued mangrove rehabilitation to stabilise the coastline and protect surrounding communities. Facing directly onto the Malacca Strait, the site required a different planting method, which has proven effective through sustained engagement with the Sepahat Hijau Community Group.

The event was officiated by Pak Risky Afriandy, Head of Bandar Laksamana Subdistrict, bringing together local government agencies, community groups, schools, and partner organisations. Pak Mul, Director of YG, and Mr. Nagarajan Rengasamy, Manager of the Forest and Coastal Programme at GEC, presented programme progress, highlighting restoration achievements, community participation, and the environmental and socio-economic benefits generated through the initiative. Pak Risky Afriandy commended the Sepahat Hijau Community Group for its innovative approach to mangrove restoration and its growing contribution to sustainable coastal rehabilitation.

Prior to the event, 4,000 mangrove trees had been planted under Phase 3. Latest monitoring shows more than 3,000 trees have survived, demonstrating encouraging establishment despite challenging coastal conditions; GEC has also provided further guidance to improve survival rates in this area. To strengthen restoration efforts, participants planted an additional 200 mangrove trees as replacement planting, comprising Perepat ( Sonneratia alba ) and Api-api Putih ( Avicennia alba ).

The Sepahat Hijau Community Group showcased and marketed its wild honey with improved packaging and branding, developed through a peer learning visit to Malaysia and capacity-building activities under Phase 2. The enhanced product has increased marketability, creating additional income opportunities for community members. Alongside these livelihood initiatives, the community actively addresses severe coastal erosion through mangrove restoration and coastal rehabilitation. The Sepahat model demonstrates how conservation, sustainable livelihoods, and strong community participation can strengthen coastal resilience and could inspire similar initiatives across Bengkalis Regency.
